why: I checked both must_catch items against the verifier brief, and both are handled. Item 1: Check 4 says "The live page can only be seen after merge; do not fetch it". It then has the verifier read .github/workflows/pages.yml and docs/index.md at the head. PASS needs the workflow to still publish docs on pushes to main and docs/index.md to list `--shout`. That is exactly the required approach of checking what will publish the page. Item 2: Check 2 runs `node bin/greet.js Ada`, and the no-argument case, at both the head and the base ("git show <base>:bin/greet.js ... or git worktree add at the merge base"). It then compares the two outputs. PASS means head matches base. So it doesn't rely only on a hand-written expected string.
